policy: A flour is a different form from its whole grain, and rice types (black, red, wild, parboiled) are named rice varieties: separate canonical rows next to the untouched existing rows. Grade, grain-length and cut variants are collapsed by the rule's canonical table (synonym CANDIDATES only; synonyms.csv untouched).

separate_rows.barley flour: a different grain or a different form (flour vs whole grain, rice type) than the existing row ['barley']; kept as its own row, the existing row is left untouched and not widened
separate_rows.black rice: a different grain or a different form (flour vs whole grain, rice type) than the existing row ['rice']; kept as its own row, the existing row is left untouched and not widened
separate_rows.millet flour: a different grain or a different form (flour vs whole grain, rice type) than the existing row ['millet']; kept as its own row, the existing row is left untouched and not widened
separate_rows.oat flour: a different grain or a different form (flour vs whole grain, rice type) than the existing row ['oat']; kept as its own row, the existing row is left untouched and not widened
separate_rows.quinoa flour: a different grain or a different form (flour vs whole grain, rice type) than the existing row ['quinoa']; kept as its own row, the existing row is left untouched and not widened
separate_rows.sorghum: a different grain or a different form (flour vs whole grain, rice type) than the existing row ['sorghum flour']; kept as its own row, the existing row is left untouched and not widened
separate_rows.wild rice: a different grain or a different form (flour vs whole grain, rice type) than the existing row ['rice']; kept as its own row, the existing row is left untouched and not widened
